cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; tipping is optional.
name: Ronda
tagline: A white town split by a dizzying gorge
summary: Ronda sits on a cliff split in two by the deep El Tajo gorge, joined by the towering Puente Nuevo bridge. Walk down to the viewpoints below the bridge, see Spain's oldest bullring, explore Moorish baths and palace gardens, and drive the white villages of the Serranía de Ronda.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal; summers are hot, winters cool for Andalusia.
arrival: Trains and buses from Málaga (about 2 hours) and Seville; about 1h45 by car from the Costa del Sol.
gettingAround: Walk the town; a car is best for the white villages.
foodTip: Rabo de toro (oxtail), Serranía game stews and Ronda wines.
buyTip: Local wines from the Serranía de Ronda and olive oil.
baseArea: La Ciudad (old town) near the bridge

items.name: Puente Nuevo
items.summary: 18th-century bridge rising 98 m from the bottom of the gorge.
items.tip: Walk the path down to the Mirador de Aldehuela.

items.name: Plaza de Toros de Ronda
items.summary: One of Spain's oldest bullrings, birthplace of modern bullfighting on foot, with a museum.
items.tip: Look round the arena and stables; no fight needed.

items.name: Arab Baths
items.summary: The best-preserved Moorish baths in Spain, with star-shaped skylights.
items.tip: Watch the short video first.

items.name: Casa del Rey Moro and the Mine
items.summary: Gardens and a Moorish stairway cut 60 m down to the river inside the gorge.
items.tip: Go down slowly; it's damp.

items.name: Alameda del Tajo and Balcón del Coño
items.summary: Park ending at a balcony hanging over the cliff edge.
items.tip: Come at sunset for the valley glow.

items.name: Setenil de las Bodegas
items.summary: White village with houses built under huge rock overhangs.
items.tip: Walk Cuevas del Sol and Cuevas de la Sombra.

items.name: Rabo de toro
items.summary: Slow-cooked oxtail stew in red wine, a Ronda speciality.
items.tip: Order with a local Serranía red.

items.name: Tapas on Plaza del Socorro
items.summary: The lively main square lined with tapas bars.
items.tip: Hop between bars, a few tapas each.

items.name: Ronda wineries
items.summary: Small wineries in the hills around town offer tastings.
items.tip: Descalzos Viejos sits in an old convent below the gorge.

cashTip: Cards are used everywhere; some places are card only.
name: The Hague
tagline: Girl with a Pearl Earring, parliament and the beach
summary: The Hague is the Netherlands' seat of government and a city of courts, palaces and a long North Sea beach. See Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring in the Mauritshuis, walk the medieval Binnenhof, visit the Escher museum and the Peace Palace, then ride the tram to Scheveningen's pier and dunes. Delft's canals are ten minutes away.
seasonNote: Summer for the beach; April for tulips at nearby Keukenhof.
arrival: Trains from Amsterdam take 50 minutes and from Schiphol 30 minutes; Rotterdam is 25 minutes away.
gettingAround: Trams cover the city and run to Scheveningen and Delft; bikes everywhere.
foodTip: Raw herring at Scheveningen, Indonesian rijsttafel (the city has a big Indo community) and poffertjes.
buyTip: Delft blue pottery in nearby Delft.

items.name: Mauritshuis
items.summary: Small, perfect gallery with Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and Rembrandt's Anatomy Lesson.
items.tip: Book a time slot online.
items.why: Dutch Golden Age at its best.

items.name: Binnenhof and Hofvijver
items.summary: Parliament complex around the medieval Knights' Hall beside a pond.
items.expect: Under renovation for years; parts are fenced.
items.tip: Photograph across the Hofvijver pond.

items.name: Escher in Het Paleis
items.summary: M. C. Escher's mind-bending prints in a former royal palace.
items.tip: Try the optical-illusion room upstairs.

items.name: Peace Palace
items.summary: Home of the International Court of Justice; the visitor centre explains its work.
items.expect: Inside only on rare guided tours.
items.tip: The visitor centre is free.

items.name: Scheveningen beach and pier
items.summary: Wide sandy beach with a pier, Ferris wheel and dune walks.
items.tip: Walk south over the dunes to quieter sand.

items.name: Madurodam
items.summary: The Netherlands in miniature: canals, windmills and Schiphol at 1:25 scale.
items.tip: Go late afternoon when it's calmer.
items.why: The whole country in an hour.

items.name: Delft
items.summary: Canal town of Vermeer and Delft blue, with leaning Oude Kerk and the Royal Delft factory.
items.tip: Climb the Nieuwe Kerk tower for the view.

items.name: Herring at Scheveningen
items.summary: Raw "Hollandse Nieuwe" herring with onions from a harbour stall.
items.tip: Hold it by the tail and eat it in a few bites.

items.name: Indonesian rijsttafel
items.summary: A spread of many small Indonesian dishes with rice, a colonial-era tradition.
items.tip: Toko and restaurants around the centre and Chinatown.

items.name: Haagse Markt
items.summary: One of Europe's largest open-air markets, with food from around the world.
items.expect: Open Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday.
items.tip: Try Surinamese roti and fresh stroopwafels.

cashTip: Carry some cash: many small restaurants and bakeries still prefer it. Round up or tip 5 to 10 percent.
name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
tagline: The medieval walled town of the Romantic Road
summary: Rothenburg ob der Tauber is Germany's best-preserved medieval walled town. Walk the covered ramparts, photograph the half-timbered Plönlein corner, climb the town hall tower, join the Night Watchman's funny evening tour and visit the year-round Christmas shop.
seasonNote: Busy with day-trippers in summer; the December Christmas market is magical.
arrival: Regional trains from Würzburg or Nuremberg with one or two changes, about 1h30 to 2h; on the Romantic Road by car.
gettingAround: Walk everything; the walled town is small.
foodTip: Schneeballen (snowball pastries), Franconian sausages and Franconian wine.

items.name: Plönlein
items.summary: Little fork in the road with a yellow half-timbered house between two towers.
items.tip: Go early or after 5 pm.

items.name: Town walls walk
items.summary: Covered wooden walkway along the ramparts with views over the roofs.
items.tip: Walk from the Spitalbastei to the Klingentor.

items.name: Town Hall Tower
items.summary: Climb 220 steps to a tiny platform with the best view in town.
items.expect: Paid; narrow ladder at the top.
items.tip: Go before 1 pm on a clear day.

items.name: Night Watchman Tour
items.summary: Funny hour-long walk with a costumed night watchman telling town history.
items.expect: English tour at 8 pm most of the year.
items.tip: Meet at the Marktplatz; pay at the end.

items.name: Medieval Crime Museum
items.summary: Museum of medieval law and punishment, from shame masks to torture tools.
items.tip: Allow time; it's bigger than it looks.

items.name: St. Jakob's Church
items.summary: Gothic church with Riemenschneider's carved Holy Blood Altar.
items.tip: Climb to the gallery behind the altar.

items.name: Burggarten
items.summary: Garden on the site of the old castle, overlooking the Tauber valley.
items.tip: Walk down into the valley for the view back up.

items.name: Käthe Wohlfahrt Christmas Village
items.summary: Year-round Christmas shop with a German Christmas museum.
items.tip: Museum is upstairs.

items.name: Schneeballen
items.summary: Balls of fried pastry strips dusted with sugar or chocolate.
items.tip: Buy a small one from a bakery like Diller's.

items.name: Franconian tavern dinner
items.summary: Half-timbered taverns with sausages, roast pork and dumplings.
items.tip: Pair with Franconian wine in a Bocksbeutel bottle.

items.name: Franconian wine
items.summary: Dry Silvaner from the Main valley in the round Bocksbeutel bottle.
items.tip: Ask for a Silvaner.

cashTip: Carry some cash: many small restaurants and bakeries still prefer it. Round up or tip 5 to 10 percent.
name: Nuremberg
tagline: Imperial castle, Christmas market and hard history
summary: Nuremberg is a walled Franconian city with a great imperial castle, Albrecht Dürer's house and Germany's most famous Christmas market. It also confronts its past: see the Nazi Party Rally Grounds and the courtroom of the Nuremberg trials, then end the day with tiny Nürnberger bratwurst and a smoky Franconian beer.
seasonNote: The Christkindlesmarkt runs from late November to Christmas Eve; summer is warm and lively.
arrival: ICE trains from Munich take 1h05 and from Berlin about 4h30; the airport is 12 minutes by U-Bahn.
gettingAround: The old town is walkable; U-Bahn and trams for the Rally Grounds.
foodTip: Nürnberger Rostbratwurst, Lebkuchen gingerbread and Franconian Rauchbier.

connections.note: Regional trains via Ansbach and Steinach.

items.name: Nuremberg Castle
items.summary: Imperial castle above the old town, with a deep well and Sinwell Tower views.
items.expect: Paid for the tower, well and palace.
items.tip: Climb the Sinwell Tower for the rooftop view.

items.name: Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds
items.summary: The unfinished Congress Hall and Zeppelin Field, with a museum on how the Nazis used them.
items.expect: Museum reopened after renovation; check opening.
items.tip: Walk around the lake to the Zeppelin tribune.

items.name: Memorium Nuremberg Trials
items.summary: Courtroom 600 where the Nazi leaders were tried, with an exhibition.
items.tip: Audio guide is excellent.

items.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
items.summary: The painter's 15th-century home and workshop.
items.tip: Join the costumed Agnes tour at weekends.

items.name: Hauptmarkt and the Schöner Brunnen
items.summary: Market square with the Frauenkirche and the golden Beautiful Fountain.
items.tip: Turn the brass ring in the fountain's grille for luck.

items.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
items.summary: Germany's biggest museum of its art and culture, including Dürer paintings and the oldest globe.
items.tip: Focus on two or three wings.

items.name: Christkindlesmarkt
items.summary: Germany's most famous Christmas market with red-and-white striped stalls.
items.expect: Late November to 24 December; very crowded.
items.tip: Weekday afternoons are calmer.

items.name: Bratwurst Röslein
items.summary: Big traditional hall grilling Nuremberg's tiny finger-sized sausages over beechwood.
items.tip: Try "drei im Weggla", three in a bread roll, from a street stand.

items.name: Lebkuchen Schmidt
items.summary: Soft spiced Nuremberg gingerbread sold in decorated tins.
items.tip: Look for Elisenlebkuchen, the finest grade.

items.name: Hausbrauerei Altstadthof
items.summary: Old-town brewpub with red beer and tours of the rock-cut beer cellars below.
items.tip: Join the Felsengänge tunnel tour, then a beer.

cashTip: The local money is the convertible mark (KM, about 2 to the euro); euros are often accepted but change comes in marks. Carry cash for small places. Prices here are shown in euros.
name: Mostar
tagline: The Old Bridge, divers and Ottoman lanes
summary: Mostar's Old Bridge arcs high over the emerald Neretva, rebuilt after the 1990s war and now a symbol of reconciliation. Watch the bridge divers leap 21 m into the river, wander the Ottoman bazaar, climb a minaret for the view, and day-trip to the Kravice waterfalls, the dervish house at Blagaj and the hill village of Počitelj.
seasonNote: July and August often reach 40°C; late spring and early autumn are best.
arrival: Trains and buses from Sarajevo take about 2 hours on one of Europe's most scenic lines; buses from Dubrovnik and Split take 3 to 4 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; a car or tour for Kravice, Blagaj and Počitelj.
foodTip: Ćevapi, Bosnian coffee, burek and Herzegovinian Žilavka wine.
buyTip: Copperware and coffee sets from Kujundžiluk bazaar.

items.name: Stari Most (Old Bridge)
items.summary: 16th-century Ottoman bridge, destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt stone by stone.
items.tip: Watch from the riverbank below at sunset.

items.name: Bridge divers
items.summary: Members of the diving club leap 21 m into the cold river once enough money is collected.
items.expect: They dive when the crowd pays.
items.tip: Watch from the west bank terrace cafés.

items.name: Kujundžiluk bazaar
items.summary: Cobbled Ottoman street of copper workshops and souvenir stalls.
items.tip: Look for real coppersmiths at work.

items.name: Koski Mehmed Pasha Mosque
items.summary: 17th-century mosque whose minaret gives the classic bridge view.
items.tip: Cover shoulders and knees inside.

items.name: Blagaj Tekke
items.summary: Dervish house beneath a cliff at the spring of the Buna river.
items.tip: Eat trout at the riverside restaurants.

items.name: Kravice Falls
items.summary: Wide curtain of waterfalls into a swimming lagoon.
items.tip: Go early on summer weekends.

items.name: Počitelj
items.summary: Ottoman hill village with a mosque and fortress tower above the Neretva.
items.tip: Climb to the tower.

items.name: War Photo Exhibition
items.summary: Photographs of the 1990s war in Mostar.
items.tip: Give it time; it explains the bridge.

items.name: Ćevapi
items.summary: Grilled minced meat fingers in fluffy somun bread with onion and kajmak.
items.tip: Tima-Irma is a well-known spot.

items.name: Bosnian coffee
items.summary: Coffee served in a copper džezva with a sugar cube and Turkish delight.
items.tip: Dip the sugar cube, then sip.

items.name: Restaurant terraces by the Neretva
items.summary: Terraces facing the bridge serving trout, stuffed vegetables and grills.
items.tip: Book a terrace table for sunset.

cashTip: The local money is the denar (about 62 to the euro); cards work in hotels and bigger restaurants, carry cash for small places. Prices here are shown in euros.
name: Ohrid
cover: Church of St. John at Kaneo
tagline: An ancient lake of churches and clear water
summary: Ohrid is a hillside old town on one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes. See the little church of St. John at Kaneo on its cliff above the water, walk up to Samuel's Fortress and the Roman theatre, see world-class Byzantine frescoes, swim from rocky coves and visit the springs and monastery of St. Naum.
seasonNote: Summer is warm and busy with swimmers; spring and autumn are calm.
arrival: Ohrid Airport has seasonal flights; buses from Skopje take 3 hours, from Tirana about 3.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; boats and buses to St. Naum.
foodTip: Ohrid trout (protected; order belvica or farmed trout instead), tavče gravče baked beans and ajvar.
buyTip: Ohrid pearls made from fish-scale lacquer, a town craft.

items.name: Church of St. John at Kaneo
items.wiki: Church of St. John at Kaneo
items.summary: Small 13th-century church on a cliff above the lake, the classic Ohrid view.
items.tip: Walk the boardwalk from the beach to reach it.

items.name: Samuel's Fortress
items.summary: Walls of the 10th-century Bulgarian tsar's fortress with views over the lake.
items.tip: Walk the ramparts end to end.

items.name: Plaošnik and St. Panteleimon
items.summary: Site of St. Clement's school, cradle of the Cyrillic script, with a rebuilt church and mosaics.
items.tip: Look for the early Christian floor mosaics.

items.name: Church of St. Sophia
items.summary: 11th-century cathedral with some of the finest medieval frescoes in the Balkans.
items.tip: Summer evening concerts are held here.

items.name: Ancient Theatre of Ohrid
items.summary: Hellenistic theatre still used for summer festival shows.
items.tip: Check the Ohrid Summer Festival program.

items.name: Monastery of St. Naum
items.summary: Monastery at the lake's southern tip with springs you can boat through.
items.tip: Take a rowing boat through the Black Drin springs.

items.name: Bay of Bones
items.summary: Reconstructed prehistoric village on stilts over the lake.
items.expect: Paid; on the road to St. Naum.
items.tip: Combine with the St. Naum trip.

items.name: Old town lakefront and beaches
items.summary: Rocky coves and swimming platforms beneath the old town.
items.expect: Water is cold even in July.
items.tip: Take a boat tour from the harbour at sunset.

items.name: Tavče gravče
items.summary: Baked beans with peppers and onions in a clay pot, the national dish.
items.tip: Order with shopska salad.

items.name: Lake fish (belvica)
items.summary: Fish from the lake grilled simply; wild Ohrid trout is protected so pick belvica or farmed trout.
items.expect: Ask where the fish comes from.
items.tip: Eat at a lakeside terrace.

items.name: Old bazaar burek
items.summary: Flaky pastry filled with cheese or meat, with yogurt, for breakfast.
items.tip: Buy from a busy bakery near the plane tree.

cashTip: Bulgaria uses the euro since 2026; cards are widely accepted. Tip about 10 percent.
name: Plovdiv
tagline: Europe's oldest living city on seven hills
summary: Plovdiv has been lived in for 8,000 years. Sit in a Roman theatre still used for concerts, walk the colourful Revival houses of the Old Town, explore the street-art district of Kapana, and climb a hill at sunset for the view over the Thracian plain. Bachkovo Monastery and the Rose Valley are short trips away.
seasonNote: Late May to early June for the Rose Valley harvest; summers are hot.
arrival: Trains and buses from Sofia take 2 to 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the old town and centre; cobbles are uneven.
foodTip: Shopska salad, kavarma stew, banitsa pastry and Mavrud red wine.
buyTip: Rose oil products and Mavrud wine.

items.name: Roman Theatre
items.summary: 2nd-century theatre on the hillside, still used for summer concerts and opera.
items.tip: See a summer show if you can.

items.name: Old Town
items.summary: Cobbled hill of brightly painted 19th-century Revival houses and museums.
items.tip: Visit Balabanov House and the Ethnographic Museum.

items.name: Kapana district
items.summary: "The Trap", a maze of lanes full of street art, craft bars and galleries.
items.tip: Come for dinner and stay for drinks.

items.name: Nebet Tepe
items.summary: Hilltop with the ruins of the oldest Thracian settlement and a city view.
items.tip: Come at sunset.

items.name: Roman Stadium
items.summary: Part of a huge Roman stadium visible below the main pedestrian street.
items.expect: Free to view; small 3D film paid.
items.tip: Have a coffee at the Dzhumaya Mosque next door.

items.name: Bachkovo Monastery
items.summary: Bulgaria's second-largest monastery, founded in 1083, with fine frescoes.
items.tip: Combine with Asen's Fortress on the way.

items.name: Rose Valley (Kazanlak)
items.summary: Valley that produces much of the world's rose oil, with a Thracian tomb at Kazanlak.
items.expect: Harvest is late May to early June.
items.tip: Join a dawn rose-picking.

items.name: Shopska salad and grill
items.summary: Tomatoes, cucumber and grated white cheese, then kebapche and kyufte from the grill.
items.tip: Pair with a rakia.

items.name: Banitsa breakfast
items.summary: Flaky filo pastry with egg and white cheese, eaten with boza or ayran.
items.tip: Buy fresh from a busy window.

items.name: Mavrud wine in Kapana
items.summary: Wine bars pouring Mavrud, the dark red grape of the Thracian valley.
items.tip: Ask for a local tasting flight.
